item.title: Top 10 AI use cases on X, Oct 26 2026
item.description:
The ten most-engaged X posts from the last 24 hours showing people actually using AI: agents buying and cancelling things safely, making phone calls, managing other agents, and building real tools and businesses.

  1. Grok Bot bought a Spotify trial and dodged a hidden prompt injection

    Layton_Gott let Grok Bot sign them up for Spotify's $1 trial and cancel it right after so the $12.99 never hit. It spotted hidden text on the checkout page telling AI agents to click an invisible button, ignored it, and asked for the card through a secure form before charging.

    @Layton_Gott on X · 1,366 likes · 49 reposts · 158,467 views

  2. A vibe-coded leaderboard became a 200-acquisition marketplace

    marclou says TrustMRR started as a vibe-coded revenue leaderboard for founders, then turned into a startup marketplace after users asked for it. It has now passed 200 acquisitions, 250,000 monthly visitors, and is his highest-margin product.

    @marclou on X · 553 likes · 10 reposts · 38,770 views

  3. Grok Bot made every phone call for a day

    ScottyBeamIO handed all their calls to Grok Bot's new calling feature. It sat through an internet provider's menu, asked for retention and got $35 a month off with email confirmation, and turned down three retention offers to cancel a phone-only gym membership.

    @ScottyBeamIO on X · 535 likes · 27 reposts · 53,428 views

  4. A goal keeper bot that manages the other agents

    Andrew Warner asked his Grok Bot why others get more from their agents, and it told him to give goals, not tasks. He made his main Grok Bot a goal keeper that sets a measurable goal for each agent and checks progress, and he shared the prompt.

    @AndrewWarner on X · 499 likes · 12 reposts · 40,155 views

  5. Grok Bot is planning its own hardware device

    Texas_Twins_Dad got "Hey Grok" to open Grok Bot voice chat through a Bluetooth speaker, then asked Grok Bot to plan a dedicated device. It laid out the design, the parts, and the cheapest place to buy each one, and the first part is on its way.

    @Texas_Twins_Dad on X · 161 likes · 4 reposts · 5,954 views

  6. Designer built a liquid-shapes 3D web tool

    aecyydesign built a browser-based React tool with Claude Code (Opus 5.5) and Toolcraft, with a custom WebGL2 path tracer and Intel's OIDN denoiser on WebGPU that exports seamless 4K loops. Every visual in the post came out of it.

    @aecyydesign on X · 154 likes · 5 reposts · 4,033 views

  7. One-click button that feeds a second brain

    Av1dlive built a Grok Bot button that works on any web page. One click sends the page to their Grok Bot, a curator agent files it into a second brain, and that agent finds patterns and turns them into ideas.

    @Av1dlive on X · 52 likes · 7 reposts · 3,191 views

  8. Grok Bot as a creator's research and outreach team

    nixeniego uses Grok Bot to deliver the most viral content in their niche every morning, mine Reddit, YouTube comments, and X for audience complaints, and find and pitch aligned sponsors, work they say used to need a $2,000-a-month assistant.

    @nixeniego on X · 19 likes · 1 reposts · 1,263 views

  9. Grok Bot for marketing, Hermes as a phone-in assistant

    JulianGoldieSEO runs both daily. Grok Bot finds 10 businesses at 7am, writes each a personal email, and drafts replies to new leads within a minute, while Hermes Agent takes phone calls, knows his projects from his Obsidian vault, and books his sessions.

    @JulianGoldieSEO on X · 17 likes · 0 reposts · 4,756 views

  10. Grok Bot runs an X account like a marketing team

    UncensoredUSA has Grok Bot handle morning story ideas, fact checks, video wraps, and posting times for their X account, so they only press the buttons. They're asking for post scheduling directly from Grok Bot next.

    @UncensoredUSA on X · 15 likes · 16 reposts · 1,332 views

item.title: Top 10 AI use cases on X, Oct 25 2026
item.description:
These are the top 10 AI use cases on X over the last 24 hours, ranked by engagement. A hands-free Hey Grok trick for iPhone dominated Sunday, alongside Claude Code builds for games, video and 3D, and Grok Bot running a TV, privacy requests and a small business.

  1. Saying Hey Grok on an iPhone

    Texas Twins Dad found a way to open Grok Bot voice chat just by saying Hey Grok, using a Shortcuts action plus iOS Vocal Shortcuts in Accessibility settings. No extra app or cost, and it works hands-free once Face ID has unlocked the phone.

    @Texas_Twins_Dad on X · 6,736 likes · 711 reposts · 1,633,127 views

  2. A Roblox game shipped in three days

    killah vibe coded a full Roblox simulator with Claude Opus 5.5, using an outside pack only for the animals and eggs, and released it in three days.

    @killahdev on X · 193 likes · 1 repost · 13,712 views

  3. Video editing for about $4 instead of $800

    Alex Scott used to pay $800 per edited video. Now Claude Code does the edit, Gemini drafts, and DaVinci Resolve finishes, at roughly $4 of AI and two hours per video, and he shared the whole setup.

    @afscott on X · 97 likes · 4 reposts · 5,553 views

  4. Grok Bot runs the TV by voice

    natalie had Claude Code on Opus 5.5 find her Samsung TV's local remote API from one photo of its About screen and write a tiny three-tool remote. Plugged into Grok Bot, a spoken sentence now opens Netflix and scrolls it.

    @realNatalieFort on X · 46 likes · 0 reposts · 1,380 views

  5. Playing music with just fingers and Grok Bot

    This user set up Grok Bot to turn finger movements into music and export it as an MP3, with no instrument involved.

    @fffuckingnerd on X · 32 likes · 2 reposts · 590 views

  6. A 3D pond story built entirely in code

    Karan Gupta built a scroll story about the Butterfly Dream paradox, a frog playing violin for a duck, with no 3D models or audio files, using Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code with three.js and the Web Audio API.

    @justkarangupta on X · 31 likes · 4 reposts · 520 views

  7. 400 delete-my-data requests sent overnight

    nexor gave Grok Bot one night to pull Samsung's list of data partners, find each privacy contact, and send deletion requests under local privacy law. By morning it reported 400 sent and 37 confirmed, with a table of replies and 30-day reminders.

    @nexor404 on X · 27 likes · 0 reposts · 554 views

  8. A Fiverr-style 3D product video with Claude

    Kirisando, with no 3D or motion design skills, had Claude Code rebuild a game controller in 3D from one photo, add water, lighting, a camera flight, an exploded view and sound, all in code. It took about an hour and four rounds of notes on the cheapest paid Claude plan.

    @kirisando on X · 19 likes · 1 repost · 414 views

  9. An agent running its own small business

    Marko describes how Alex Finn's Grok Bot agent Milo built and monetized a directory of AI agent use cases, keeps it updated daily from Google, Reddit, X and LinkedIn, and pings him when sponsors pay.

    @Marko_Poly on X · 17 likes · 2 reposts · 612 views

  10. An old Echo Dot turned into a custom voice assistant

    Teles jailbroke a 2016 Echo Dot, trained their own wake word model, and connected it to Home Assistant, running GPT realtime through a Codex subscription.

    @teles_dev on X · 13 likes · 0 reposts · 515 views

item.title: Top 10 AI use cases on X, Oct 24 2026
item.description:
These are the top 10 AI use cases on X over the last 24 hours, ranked by engagement. Saturday was quieter, led by Claude Code doing real security and editing work, plus Grok Bot running investment research, a newsletter, a website and a personal command center.

  1. Claude Code finds the photos an iPhone never really deleted

    Deni asked Claude Code (on Opus 5.5) to run a quick security check while his iPhone backed up to his laptop. It found years of photos still hidden inside his iMessage, WhatsApp and Telegram chats, plus five old unencrypted iPhone backups in a hidden Windows folder, including a passport photo and bank screenshots he thought were gone.

    @0xDeniAi on X · 73 likes · 6 reposts · 4,496 views

  2. A math video finally edited by a Claude Code pipeline

    Po-Shen Loh had a year-old recording explaining why e is natural that nobody had time to edit. He built a full video editing pipeline in Claude Code and finally released it, all real footage.

    @PoShenLoh on X · 61 likes · 12 reposts · 4,550 views

  3. Claude audits its own game and finds the crash bug

    0xbobaa gave Claude Code the read-only repo for Skyhold, a city builder made with Opus, and asked it to attack it. In under six minutes it found 13 issues, including a malformed URL that had already crashed the live server twice and unchecked leaderboard scores, and both were patched the same day.

    @0xbobaaa on X · 69 likes · 3 reposts · 2,690 views

  4. A daily investment report built from an X List

    zaimiri gave Grok Bot an X List of investors they trust. Every morning it scans their last 24 hours of posts, labels each position as buy, hold, sell or watch with the post as evidence, flags agreement and disagreement, and compares it with yesterday's report.

    @zaimiri on X · 65 likes · 1 repost · 1,847 views

  5. A pizza simulator from one Opus 5.5 prompt

    Mr Tactical asked Claude Opus 5.5 to build a pizza simulator game and shared the playable result, asking followers whether it should become a full game.

    @MrTacticalX on X · 56 likes · 2 reposts · 4,036 views

  6. An industrial robot you can take apart in the browser

    Valentin had Claude (Opus 5.5) build an interactive 6-axis KUKA robot with every part labelled. It stacks cubes, writes on the floor with a marker, and lets you open a joint to see the motor and gearbox, using KUKA's real specs with simulated motion.

    @martynov014 on X · 34 likes · 4 reposts · 781 views

  7. Grok Bot as a personal Wall Street newsletter

    Ardullo told Grok Bot which stocks, earnings and big moves matter to their portfolio. Now it checks on its own and only pings them when something is worth looking at, instead of opening five apps every morning.

    @RafelineK on X · 16 likes · 2 reposts · 255 views

  8. A Grok Bot wingman named My Man

    Lfleezy's Grok Bot mapped a Disney Springs bar crawl and emailed the itinerary, dug through county public records, analyzed their X analytics to help restore monetization, and sends fresh post ideas every Monday for their dogs and veterans.

    @LFleezy23 on X · 13 likes · 1 repost · 342 views

  9. A first website that Grok Bot now runs

    Erinn had never coded, so Grok Build wrote her first website, then she handed the site to Grok Bot. It now pulls her top X posts and videos, makes printable recipe cards in English, Japanese and Spanish, watches her contact form and publishes changes on request.

    @ErinnFL on X · 11 likes · 0 reposts · 351 views

  10. A whole-life command center in Grok Bot

    MAGS built an animated hub in Grok Bot that links net worth, a property inventory, a budget, estate tracking and tasks, where changing one value updates every layer. They shared it as a free template.

    @TAftermath2020 on X · 9 likes · 1 repost · 924 views

item.title: Top 10 AI use cases on X, Oct 23 2026
item.description:
The ten most-engaged X posts from the last 24 hours showing people actually putting AI to work, from personal agents handling refunds and scam texts to one-shot coding projects. Ranked by likes, reposts and views.

  1. Racing Claude to fix a broken Linux box

    Dave Plummer's Linux system got stuck, so he asked Claude to fix it from the command line while he fixed it himself with his own task manager tool. Both landed on the same runaway process and killed it; his command won by a second or two.

    @davepl1968 on X · 135 likes · 7 reposts · 5,769 views

  2. Grok Bot as an everything app

    This user texts one Grok Bot to read email and calendar, book and reschedule, order things, chase returns until refunds land, and keep live pages for net worth and bills. It learns how they like each task done and repeats it as a routine.

    @GrokletMascot on X · 67 likes · 18 reposts · 3,312 views

  3. Agent applied to a startup program, made a LinkedIn too

    He dropped the Grok for Startups link into his Grok Bot and asked it to apply. When the form required LinkedIn, the bot created and filled out a LinkedIn profile, pulled verification codes from its own inbox, and submitted the application.

    @Texas_Twins_Dad on X · 53 likes · 2 reposts · 6,436 views

  4. An AI agent with its own email as a scheduler

    Parmita Mishra gave her AI agent, Sugar, its own email address, and it now handles meeting scheduling for her company Precigenetics in place of Calendly.

    @parmita on X · 48 likes · 2 reposts · 3,011 views

  5. An interactive Cybercab factory line

    Konstantin Saifoulline had Grok Bot use Claude Opus 5.5 to build a live, take-apart simulation of Tesla's unboxed Cybercab production line, with six sections assembling at once and a car every 60 seconds.

  6. Meta Muse caught a hidden $70 fee

    After a car seat return, Meta Muse noticed on its own that the refund was $70 short from a restocking fee, then gave David Zagury Amazon's number and a script with his order number. One call got the $70 back.

    Kris Shan gave Grok Bot read-only access to his mom's email and texts. It checks senders, links, and contacts, moves fakes like a new-number money request and a phony Chase alert into a separate folder before she sees them, and tells him what it stopped.

    Sarvasv Kulpati is posting daily mini projects on a vibe-codeable ESP32 gadget. Day one is a Flappy Bird clone you control by screaming, written in one shot by Codex.

  9. 25 Framer templates in 14 days

    A designer built close to 25 free Framer website templates in two weeks using a custom Claude Code skill pack and workflow, without the Framer MCP.

    @CreativeDima on X · 11 likes · 1 repost · 409 views

  10. Flight rebooked and dentist moved, hands-free

    Nick's Grok Bot found a cheaper flight, called the airline to switch dates and talked them out of the change fee. It then spotted a dentist conflict, called to reschedule, and updated his calendar.

    @thecsguy on X · 11 likes · 1 repost · 413 views

item.title: Top 10 AI use cases on X, Oct 22 2026
item.description:
These are the top 10 AI use cases on X over the last 24 hours, ranked by engagement. Thursday leaned hard into Grok Bot doing real work: a lead-generation site, a portable second brain, a family assistant and a parking-ticket fight, plus Claude and Codex building a game and developer tools.

  1. A Grok Bot lead site pulls in crane rental requests

    Marko breaks down a podcast demo where Grok Bot found an under-served service in Laredo, bought an $11 domain, built the site, wired up Google Analytics and Search Console, and now sends a weekly ranking report. The site pulled in about $35,000 worth of crane rental requests in its first month (the value of the jobs, not revenue).

    Vinay moved his fiancée's second brain (a GitHub repo of notes plus an Obsidian vault) off Claude Code on a home Mac Mini and onto Grok Bot, which runs on its own cloud computer, so it doesn't go offline when she travels. She now talks to it by voice from her phone, and he uses Grok Bot to drive his home server.

    @vinayp10 on X · 301 likes · 14 reposts · 144,630 views

    XFreeze replied to @bot with one line, and Grok Bot used his past history to build a dashboard covering all 14 Starship flights, with launch dates, booster catches, reentries, outcomes, charts and a Flight 15 preview.

item.title: Top 10 AI use cases on X, Oct 21 2026
item.description:
These are the top 10 AI use cases on X over the last 24 hours, ranked by engagement. Wednesday was dominated by Grok Bot builds, from fraud cleanup and storage templates to agent dashboards, plus Claude Opus 5.5 making games, video edits and a custom TV interface.

  1. A Grok Bot catches credit fraud for a friend

    He says a Grok Bot he built for a friend turned up seven fraudulent accounts a scammer had opened in the friend's name, more than $65,000 in defaulted credit, and the bot is now working to get them cleared. This is his own account and he links to the bot in the post.

    @BrianRoemmele on X · 474 likes · 63 reposts · 5,023,174 views

  2. A Grok Bot template that offloads storage to Google Drive

    He built a Grok Bot template called Drive Vault that moves old raw files to Google Drive when the bot's computer runs low on space, checks each upload, then frees the space so long video jobs keep running. It also uploads finished videos to Drive and sends a one-tap link for getting them onto a phone.

    @XFreeze on X · 387 likes · 46 reposts · 23,116 views

  3. Opus 5.5 builds a post-apocalyptic open world

    He says Claude Opus 5.5 built an unfinished post-apocalyptic open-world game for him in about 17 hours using Blender and the Godot engine. He puts the cost at $118 plus 17 hours of his weekly usage.

    @badboyfoxy on X · 205 likes · 4 reposts · 14,396 views

  4. Claude edits a drone-footage reel

    He plugged in a hard drive of drone footage and asked Claude Opus 5.5 for a reel. Claude identified the location as Srirangam, checked the facts, picked a song and built every animation, with him approving the final cut.

    @tnexplorer on X · 202 likes · 10 reposts · 20,572 views

  5. Grok Bot builds a live crypto trading terminal

    He had Grok Bot build an AI trading terminal with six agents that scan new token pairs, run rug checks and execute trades live. He claims it turned $19.63 into $9,179.40; that figure is his own and not independently verified.

    @0xCristal on X · 126 likes · 14 reposts · 15,268 views

  6. A Grok Bot class built and shipped in 48 hours

    He built and launched a Grok Bot class in 48 hours using Grok Bot itself, wired to Cloudflare, Resend, Stripe, Gmail and Cursor, with a team of bots running around the clock. He says 665 people have signed up so far.

    She had already built a dashboard to track her 15 Grok Bot agents and is now rebuilding it with Pages to show blocked, busy and inactive bots. Next on her list are a live dashboard tracking each X post against her median and a growth dashboard by platform.

  8. Seven setup lessons behind 25 hours a week saved

    He shares the Grok Bot setup habits he credits with saving about 25 hours a week, such as handing over outcomes instead of steps, turning repeated asks into routines, and splitting recurring jobs across specialist bots. The full list is in his quoted post.

    @Michael_Fenech_ on X · 32 likes · 5 reposts · 7,375 views

  9. A mom's morning email triage

    His mom, who he says barely texted until 2015, now uses Grok Bot every morning to summarize her email and flag which messages are worth answering.

    @CostaKapo on X · 23 likes · 0 reposts · 740 views

  10. Claude Code turns an old smart TV into a custom OS

    He gave Claude Code his Android TV's IP address on the same Wi-Fi, and in one evening it disabled 19 preloaded ad and tracker packages, built a new home screen he calls DreamOS, added remote sounds, and installed a VPN and Steam Link.

item.title: Top 10 AI use cases on X, Oct 19 2026
item.description:
These are the top 10 AI use cases on X from the last day, ranked by engagement. Hacking everyday hardware with AI led the way, from Claude Code agents on a car dashboard to a vibe-coded ad-free TV and a robot vacuum brought back from the dead. Solo game builds, a Hermes agent setup, and Grok Bot handling a flight refund, a Basecamp setup and Tesla charging round out the list.

  1. Claude Code agents on a car's CarPlay screen

    Codez plugged an Android CarPlay box into a BMW and had Claude Code on Opus 5.5 work out how CarPlay draws its screen. It then ran four Claude Code agents in tmux and streamed them to the dashboard, so Codez can switch between agents and approve code changes from the driver's seat while parked.

    @0xCodez on X · 423 likes · 33 reposts · 34,425 views

  2. A vibe-coded TV home screen with no ads

    This builder used AI to make a custom home screen for a $50 Xiaomi TV Stick, with no ads or tracking and a 3D model of the apartment. One button changes the real lights, and a Movie mode dims them and opens Netflix. Both apps are open source.

    @0xProbabillity on X · 398 likes · 20 reposts · 28,984 views

  3. A multiplayer MMO drawn entirely in text characters

    Smallzero vibe coded a full multiplayer RPG MMO where every object on screen is an ASCII character. The post shows the game running in a video but doesn't say which AI tools were used.

    @Smallzero on X · 341 likes · 19 reposts · 14,055 views

  4. A solo cozy fishing game with one job per tool

    Sorenxet built a fishing game alone using Tripo for every 3D model, Claude Code connected to Blender to prep and animate the models with Opus 5.5, and Unity 6 for the world and game systems. After each step Sorenxet plays the game and fixes exactly one thing.

    @sorenxet on X · 165 likes · 5 reposts · 8,491 views

  5. Remixing GTA 5, Spider-Man and the Hulk in one city

    Deni used Opus 5.5 with REA, a free open-source tool, to have Claude trace the code behind game mechanics like Spider-Man's swing and the Hulk's stomp. Claude wrote each rule down and rebuilt it in Godot with new art, and two hours later all three were in one New York scene.

    @0xDeniAi on X · 63 likes · 4 reposts · 3,540 views

  6. One Hermes agent for work and one for personal projects

    Somewhere replaced separate Codex and Claude Code sessions with a single Hermes Agent for work at Actual and another for personal projects, and says it made iterating on work much faster, like having a mind-reader.

    @somewheresy on X · 42 likes · 2 reposts · 1,552 views

  7. Reviving a dead robot vacuum after its cloud shut down

    Mika had Claude Code on Opus 5.5 reverse-engineer how a $400 robot vacuum talked to its maker's now-dead servers, then built a local server to control it. It now cleans at 8:30 every weekday, and Mika tested it offline over local Wi-Fi before leaving it running.

    @mika_systems on X · 41 likes · 5 reposts · 1,273 views

  8. Grok Bot files a flight refund faster than the airline app

    Zack asked Grok Bot to find and fill out the refund form for a changed, delayed flight. It finished and the email confirmation arrived before Zack was even done in the airline's app.

    @BLKMDL3 on X · 36 likes · 0 reposts · 2,814 views

  9. Grok and Claude working as a team inside Basecamp

    Andy Meadows asked Grok by voice while driving to set up the Basecamp command-line tool on Grok's own computer, and within 10 minutes it was reading and writing to the Basecamp project. Now Grok and Claude collaborate with Andy there like a team, after Notion didn't work out.

    @andymeadows on X · 18 likes · 1 repost · 51,463 views

  10. Grok Bot builds a Tesla road-trip prep skill
